name: Login with Clerk
summary: Signing in with Clerk on Next.js: Clerk's own components for sign-up and sign-in by emailed code or Google, organizations and invitations, and the app's users in Postgres from Clerk's webhooks.
runsOn: A Next.js app and the real ClerkJS in Chromium, with Postgres in Docker
shows: The real `<SignIn/>`, `<SignUp/>`, `<UserButton/>` and `<OrganizationSwitcher/>` against danwo's Clerk emulator: emailed codes, Google's consent screen, invitations
A second person in a second browser: Bob opens the invitation email and joins Ada's organization
Invariants that read Clerk and Postgres: one app user per Clerk user, the same memberships on both sides, every unsigned webhook refused
`danwo matrix` faulting Clerk's Backend API, its webhooks (duplicate, late, forged, stale) and the app's SQL, with `CLERK_LOGIN_BUG` switches that turn a safeguard off
